question: Which tool is primarily used by a plumber to grip and turn metal pipes and fittings? 🚰
explanation: Awesome! A pipe wrench has adjustable, toothed jaws that easily grip round metal pipes so the plumber can loosen or tighten them. 🛠️
hint: This heavy metal tool is adjustable to fit different sizes of pipes.

question: What lightweight material is most commonly used for modern household water pipes because it does not rust? 💧
explanation: Brilliant! PVC (Polyvinyl Chloride) is a durable plastic that is widely used in plumbing because it is rust-proof, cheap, and easy to cut. 🚿
hint: It is a type of hard plastic often grey or white in color.

question: What should a plumber wrap around the threads of a pipe before joining it to prevent water leaks? 🚰
explanation: Perfect! Teflon tape is a white, non-sticky tape wrapped around pipe threads to create a watertight seal and prevent leaks. 💧
hint: It is a thin white tape specially made for plumbing threads.

question: Why is a U-trap (or P-trap) installed in the drainage pipe under a kitchen sink? 🍽️
options: To block foul smells from coming back up 👃
answer: To block foul smells from coming back up 👃
explanation: Excellent! The U-trap holds a small amount of water that acts as a seal, preventing bad sewer gases from entering the kitchen. 🏡
hint: Think about what happens to the smelly gases in the sewer pipe.

question: If a bathroom tap is constantly dripping water when closed, which small part usually needs to be replaced? 🚰
explanation: Great job! A worn-out rubber washer inside the tap stops sealing the water properly, causing the tap to drip. Replacing it fixes the leak! 🔧
hint: It is a tiny, flat, circular piece of rubber.

question: Which cutting tool is best suited for cutting thick PVC pipes in a straight line? 🪚
explanation: Awesome! A hacksaw has a fine-toothed blade that cuts smoothly through plastic and metal pipes without breaking them. 🛠️
hint: It is a hand saw commonly used for cutting metal or hard plastic.

question: What is the very first step you must take before repairing a leaking water pipe in your house? 🛑
options: Turn off the main water supply valve 🚰
Put a bucket under the pipe 🪣
answer: Turn off the main water supply valve 🚰
explanation: Spot on! Always turn off the main water valve first so that water stops flowing; otherwise, you will flood the house! 🌊
hint: You need to stop the water at its source.

question: Which plumbing fitting is used to connect two pipes together in a straight line? ➖
explanation: Fantastic! A coupling is a short tube used to connect two pipes of the same diameter in a straight line. 🪈
hint: Think of a word that means bringing two things together.

question: In basic electrical wiring, what tool is specifically designed to safely remove the plastic insulation from a wire? ⚡
explanation: Brilliant! A wire stripper cuts through the plastic coating without damaging the copper wires inside. 🔌
hint: Its name describes exactly what it does to the wire.

question: What versatile digital device is used to measure voltage, current, and resistance in electrical circuits? 📟
explanation: Perfect! A multimeter is an essential electronic tool that combines several measurement functions in one unit to troubleshoot circuits. 🔌
hint: It has 'multi' in its name because it measures many things.

question: According to standard color codes in Indian electrical wiring, what color is the 'Earth' (Ground) wire? 🌍
explanation: Excellent! The Earth wire is typically green (or green with a yellow stripe) and safely carries leaked current to the ground. 🏡
hint: Think of the color of nature and grass.

question: Which wire brings the active electrical current from the power grid into your household appliances? ⚡
explanation: Great job! The Live (or Phase) wire carries the high voltage current and is usually red or brown. Always handle it with extreme care! 🔌
hint: It is also known as the 'Phase' wire.

question: What does MCB stand for in a modern electrical distribution board? 🏠
explanation: Awesome! An MCB is an automatic switch that turns off the electricity when there is an overload or short circuit, protecting your home from fires. 🛡️
hint: It breaks the circuit when there is danger.

question: What happens to a traditional fuse when too much electric current flows through the circuit? 🔥
options: It melts and breaks the circuit ⚡
answer: It melts and breaks the circuit ⚡
explanation: Spot on! The fuse has a thin wire that melts easily. When too much current flows, it melts and stops the electricity, keeping appliances safe! 🛡️
hint: It sacrifices itself to save the other appliances.

question: Why do electricians use screwdrivers and pliers with rubber or thick plastic handles? 🪛
options: Because rubber is an insulator and prevents electric shocks 🛑
answer: Because rubber is an insulator and prevents electric shocks 🛑
explanation: Fantastic! Rubber and plastic do not conduct electricity, so the handles protect the electrician from dangerous electric shocks. ⚡
hint: Think about how electricity travels.

question: Which small tool has a tiny bulb inside and is used to check if a socket has active electrical current? 💡
explanation: Brilliant! A line tester looks like a small screwdriver. When touched to a live wire, a tiny neon bulb inside lights up to warn you of live current! ⚡
hint: It 'tests' if the line is live.

question: What should you use to securely cover joined electrical wires so they don't cause a short circuit? 🔌
explanation: Perfect! Electrical tape is made of vinyl that insulates the wires, preventing the electricity from leaking out and causing sparks or shocks. ⚡
hint: It is usually a stretchy black tape used specifically by electricians.

question: In a standard 3-pin plug, what is the purpose of the top, thicker pin? 🔌
options: It connects to the Earth wire for safety 🌍
It holds the plug tightly in the wall 🧱
answer: It connects to the Earth wire for safety 🌍
explanation: Excellent! The thicker top pin is the Earth pin. It is longer so it connects first, grounding the appliance to protect you from shocks before power flows! 🛡️
hint: It connects to the green wire.

question: If your mixer grinder suddenly stops working while grinding heavy spices, what should you check first? 🍛
options: The overload protection switch at the bottom 🔄
answer: The overload protection switch at the bottom 🔄
explanation: Great job! Most mixer grinders have a red overload switch at the bottom that pops out if the motor gets too hot. Pressing it back in resets the machine! ⚙️
hint: Look underneath the base of the machine.

question: What component inside an electric iron gets intensely hot to help press clothes? 👕
explanation: Awesome! The heating element is a special coil of high-resistance wire (usually Nichrome) that converts electricity directly into heat. 🔥
hint: Its name describes what it does: it creates heat.

question: Which part of an electric iron automatically turns off the heat when it gets too hot? 🌡️
explanation: Spot on! The thermostat acts like a brain for the iron, measuring the temperature and cutting off power to prevent clothes from burning. 👕
hint: It shares part of its name with a thermometer.

question: If a ceiling fan makes a loud squeaking or grinding noise while spinning, what does it most likely need? 🌀
options: Lubrication (oil or grease) in the bearings 🛢️
answer: Lubrication (oil or grease) in the bearings 🛢️
explanation: Fantastic! The metal ball bearings dry out over time. Adding a few drops of lubricating oil makes the fan spin silently and smoothly again! ⚙️
hint: Think about what fixes squeaky hinges on a door.

question: If a toaster does not pop the bread up when it's done, which mechanism is likely faulty? 🍞
explanation: Brilliant! The toaster relies on a timer and a mechanical spring to push the toast up. If they get stuck or break, your toast might burn! 🛠️
hint: Think about what pushes things upwards.

question: What should you absolutely NEVER use to put out a fire caused by an electrical short circuit? 🔥
explanation: Perfect! Water conducts electricity. Throwing water on an electrical fire can send a deadly electric shock right back to you! Always use sand or a CO2 extinguisher. ⚡
hint: It is liquid and conducts electricity.

question: Which type of fire extinguisher is safest and most effective for putting out electrical fires? 🧯
explanation: Excellent! CO2 is a non-conductive gas that chokes the fire by removing oxygen, making it the safest choice for electrical fires. 🛡️
hint: It contains the gas we exhale when we breathe.

question: What is the absolute first thing you must do if you see someone getting an electric shock? ⚡
options: Grab their arm to pull them away 🤝
Turn off the main power switch 🛑
answer: Turn off the main power switch 🛑
explanation: Great job! Always disconnect the power source immediately. If you touch the person while the power is on, you will get shocked too! 🛡️
hint: You need to stop the flow of electricity at its source.

question: Why is it dangerous to turn on an electrical switch with wet hands? 🖐️
options: It will make the switch dirty 🧽
Water conducts electricity and can give you a shock ⚡
answer: Water conducts electricity and can give you a shock ⚡
explanation: Awesome! Tap water contains minerals that conduct electricity perfectly, creating a direct path from the switch into your body. Always dry your hands! 🚿
hint: Think about how water interacts with electric current.

question: What is the systematic process of finding the root cause of a problem in a broken machine called? 🔍
explanation: Spot on! Troubleshooting means logically checking each part of a machine step-by-step until you find and fix the exact problem. ⚙️
hint: It means 'shooting' down 'trouble'.

question: Which tool is used to heat and join small electronic components onto a printed circuit board (PCB)? 📻
explanation: Fantastic! A soldering iron melts a special metal wire (solder) to create strong electrical connections between tiny components. 🔬
hint: It rhymes with 'smoldering'.

question: What is the metal alloy wire that melts and acts like 'metal glue' during soldering? 🔧
explanation: Brilliant! Solder is usually a mix of tin and lead that melts easily and cools quickly to form a strong, conductive joint on circuit boards. ⚡
hint: It shares its name with the tool used to melt it.

question: If a light bulb in your room is constantly flickering, what is the most common cause? 💡
options: A loose electrical connection in the holder 🔌
Too much oxygen in the room 💨
answer: A loose electrical connection in the holder 🔌
explanation: Perfect! A loose wire or a bulb not screwed in tightly disrupts the flow of electricity, causing the light to flicker on and off. 🛠️
hint: Electricity is struggling to flow smoothly.

question: What is the function of a voltage stabilizer used with appliances like refrigerators and TVs? 📺
options: To protect the appliance from sudden voltage fluctuations ⚡
answer: To protect the appliance from sudden voltage fluctuations ⚡
explanation: Excellent! Stabilizers ensure that the appliance receives a steady amount of electricity, protecting sensitive motors and chips from high voltage spikes! 🛡️
hint: It 'stabilizes' the power.

question: What protective gear should you always wear on your hands when doing heavy plumbing or cutting metal? 🧤
explanation: Great job! Heavy-duty safety gloves protect your hands from sharp metal edges, hot pipes, and chemical burns while working in the workshop. 🛠️
hint: They are specially designed for tough workshop tasks.

question: What unit of measurement is used to show how much electric power an appliance like a heater or bulb consumes? 💡
explanation: Awesome! Watts (W) measure the rate of power consumption. For example, a 1000W iron uses much more power than a 10W LED bulb! 🔌
hint: Think of James Watt, the famous engineer.

question: What type of electrical current is supplied to our homes from the city power grid? 🏙️
explanation: Spot on! The power grid provides Alternating Current (AC) because it can travel long distances efficiently, unlike the DC current from a battery. 🔌
hint: It is abbreviated as 'AC'.

question: What is a major warning sign that an electrical socket is overloaded and dangerous? ⚠️
options: The socket gets hot and smells like burning plastic 🔥
The socket makes a musical sound 🎵
answer: The socket gets hot and smells like burning plastic 🔥
explanation: Fantastic! An overloaded socket draws too much current, which generates excess heat that melts the plastic. Unplug devices immediately if this happens! 🛑
hint: It involves heat and a bad smell.

question: Which highly conductive metal is most commonly found inside household electrical wires? ⚡
explanation: Brilliant! Copper is widely used in wiring because it is an excellent conductor of electricity, flexible, and much more affordable than silver or gold! 🔌
hint: It is a reddish-brown metal.

question: What is the primary function of an exhaust fan installed in a kitchen? 🍳
options: To pull smoke, moisture, and odors out of the room 🌬️
answer: To pull smoke, moisture, and odors out of the room 🌬️
explanation: Perfect! An exhaust fan creates ventilation by sucking hot air, smoke, and cooking smells outside, keeping the kitchen fresh and safe. 🏡
hint: It 'exhausts' the bad air.

question: If you need to connect two plumbing pipes at a 90-degree corner, which fitting do you use? 📐
explanation: Excellent! An elbow fitting bends the pipe system around corners smoothly without leaking. It looks just like the bent elbow of your arm! 🪈
hint: It is named after a joint in your arm.

question: What is the purpose of a 'schematic diagram' in electronics repair? 🗺️
options: To show the price of parts 💵
To provide a map of how all electrical components connect 📻
To list the colors of the machine 🎨
To show the history of the appliance 📜
answer: To provide a map of how all electrical components connect 📻
explanation: Great job! A schematic diagram acts like a roadmap, showing the technician exactly how wires and components are supposed to connect in the circuit. 🛠️
hint: It works like a map for electricians.

question: What is the role of the large capacitor attached to a ceiling fan motor? 🌀
options: To give the motor the initial extra power needed to start spinning ⚡
To hold the fan to the ceiling 🔩
answer: To give the motor the initial extra power needed to start spinning ⚡
explanation: Awesome! A fan motor needs a large jolt of energy to start moving from a dead stop. The capacitor stores and releases this burst of energy! ⚙️
hint: It acts like a temporary power booster.

question: How often should the dust filters in a room air conditioner (AC) be cleaned to maintain efficiency? ❄️
explanation: Spot on! Cleaning the AC filters monthly prevents dust blockage. A clean filter allows air to flow easily, cooling the room faster and saving electricity! 🌬️
hint: It should be done fairly often, about 12 times a year.

question: If the water drains very slowly out of your bathroom sink, what is the most likely problem? 🚰
options: There is a blockage of hair and soap in the drain pipe 🚿
answer: There is a blockage of hair and soap in the drain pipe 🚿
explanation: Fantastic! Over time, hair and soap scum build up inside the U-trap and pipes, causing a blockage. A plunger or cleaning the trap will fix it! 🛠️
hint: Something is stopping the water from flowing freely.

question: What piece of protective equipment MUST you wear to protect your eyes when drilling holes in a concrete wall? 🧱
explanation: Brilliant! Drilling creates dangerous flying dust and sharp concrete chips. Safety goggles wrap around your eyes to protect them from serious injury. 🛠️
hint: They are clear glasses that seal around your eyes.

question: What does 'Preventive Maintenance' mean when caring for household appliances? ⚙️
options: Regularly cleaning and checking them to prevent future breakdowns 🧼
Waiting for it to break before looking at it 🛠️
answer: Regularly cleaning and checking them to prevent future breakdowns 🧼
explanation: Perfect! Preventive maintenance means taking care of machines *before* they break. Oiling a fan or cleaning a filter extends the life of the appliance! 🛡️
hint: It means preventing problems before they happen.

question: Which tool is best for tightening or loosening a screw with a cross-shaped slot on its head? ➕
explanation: Excellent! The Phillips-head screwdriver is specially designed to fit snugly into cross-shaped screws, preventing the tool from slipping out while turning. 🪛
hint: It is named after an inventor and matches a 'plus' sign shape.

question: What is the primary function of the compressor in a kitchen refrigerator? 🧊
options: To make ice cubes perfectly square 🧊
To pump the refrigerant gas through the cooling system ⚙️
To turn on the internal light 💡
answer: To pump the refrigerant gas through the cooling system ⚙️
explanation: Great job! The compressor is the 'heart' of the fridge. It pumps the cooling gas through the coils, pulling heat out of the fridge to keep your food cold. ❄️
hint: It compresses and pushes the cooling gas around.

question: Why should electrical appliances be kept away from water sinks and bathtubs? 🛁
options: Water will wash off their paint 🎨
If they fall in water, it can cause a deadly electric shock ⚡
They will sink to the bottom ⚓
answer: If they fall in water, it can cause a deadly electric shock ⚡
explanation: Awesome! Because water conducts electricity, dropping a plugged-in appliance (like a hairdryer) into water will electrify the water, which is extremely dangerous! 🛑
hint: Water and electricity are a deadly combination.

question: When working in a workshop, why is it important to keep the floor clear of tools and cables? 🧹
options: To make the room look pretty ✨
To prevent tripping, falling, and serious injuries 🚫
To hide the tools from others 🙈
To make it easier to dance 💃
answer: To prevent tripping, falling, and serious injuries 🚫
explanation: Spot on! A clean, organized workspace is a safe workspace. Tripping over a wire while holding heavy tools or working near machines can cause severe accidents. 🛡️
hint: Think about what happens if you don't look where you're walking.

question: If you need to change a burnt-out ceiling light bulb, what is the safest first step? 💡
options: Turn off the light switch and ensure the power is cut 🛑
Use a wet towel to hold the bulb 🧽
Break the old glass bulb first 🔨
answer: Turn off the light switch and ensure the power is cut 🛑
explanation: Fantastic! Safety first! Always turn off the switch to ensure no electricity is flowing to the holder before you touch the bulb. ⚡
hint: You must make sure there is no active electricity flowing.
